findings.text: §47 states that the older review was returned "as already in flight" because it was complete and only waiting for promotion, and its Deliverable's third sentence ("A review whose own work is complete and which is only waiting for promotion never counts as in flight") is presented as the change; but the compose gate already implements exactly that: `recovery_review_dispatch._standing_plan_review` skips any review whose record is stored and readable via `_delivered_plan_review` (`reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:2436`, `:2459`; docstring "Once its record is stored and readable the review has delivered … it does not hold the next round's compose"), so the pointer's phase is not what decides and the sentence adds nothing — what compose lacks is the version/coverage condition the section names first

findings.reason: without a bound distinguishing "not yet" from "never", the fix converts a refusal into a queue stall that another section's done-when forbids.
findings.text: §48 requires a `review-self` request whose record "cannot yet be read" to be "kept waiting, not refused", with no expiry, while §46 requires a promotion slot to take the next waiting request within seconds and measures "an oldest wait under 30 minutes while the queue is non-empty" (plan.html:245); a request whose record never arrives therefore blocks the queue head indefinitely and fails §46's own live measure, and the plan declares no relation between the two sections

findings.reason: the gate cannot fail on the failure mode the endpoint creates, so the section's measure proves only the happy direction.
findings.text: §48's two cases cover "record arrives late" and "record absent right now", but none covers a record that never arrives, and none asserts the request is eventually refused or released, so an implementation that parks the request forever passes both cases and the negative control

findings.reason: an unimplemented limb ships green, and every plan edit that touches one unit would force a needless full re-review instead of reusing a covering review.
findings.text: §47's Deliverable has two limbs — current version, "or reads every unit the request needs covered" — and its cases exercise only the version limb (stale N, current version). No case plants a review of an older version that already covers the request's units and requires that one to be returned, so an implementation that compares versions alone passes all three

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: a finding — both sections' Why paragraphs cite run ids that resolve to no run directory, while their near neighbours do resolve.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §48's two cases never bound the wait it creates, so an implementation that waits forever passes the section's own gate.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — both sections write their gate log to the plan's evidence fragment, the same durable convention §43-§46 use.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no plan labels, stage names or ticket numbers reach any symbol or comment in either section; the prose names mechanisms (`promotion-requested`, `review-self`) that the code already uses.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §47's stated discriminator (a review only waiting for promotion) is already the shipped behaviour, so the plan misjudges which condition compose fails on; and §48's unbounded wait contradicts §46's drain bound.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §47 names compose-freshness and §48 names a review's promotion waiting for its record; neither carries a second deliverable.
